description: We are two 2nd year undergraduate students pursuing Astrophysics. Our interests include Physics, Space, and learning to code currently we are both developing our skills in python.
summary: Our concept is taking previous health collecting devices and looking to improve what is available currently to make health safety more suitable for deep space missions. The current problem we are investigating is the time delay of deep space missions. If a health crisis were to occur a communication delay can be fatal. Our concept is having continuous data collection using an ECG patch connected to a smart watch display. This would mimic a 911 operator's software for assessing calls or act as a portable medical database with files that are easily accessible to the astronauts. This addresses the challenge of time delayed communications and how efficient, simple, and informative medical information can be vital to a mission. This is not meant to replace the medical team on the ground, rather it is meant to play as ‘interim’ doctor until medical teams can get in contact. The importance is highlighted in the safety of those taking advances in science. In doing so allows for advancement in deep space missions and pushing boundaries in future space missions and our understanding of health in unfamiliar environments.
details:
This is meant to be a very simple visual aid that uses color assigned to vitals to denote status. If an anomaly occurs it provides a simple yes or no questionnaire to diagnose the issue. When deemed necessary as a medical crisis occurs it provides a simple step by step data sheet to allow for self aid or crew member assistance while still contacting medical teams back on earth for assistance. This will also include a self reporting feature allowing for simple check ups as the astronaut feels is needed for their health.

Our project works by using a multivital ECG patch that would track vitals for the heart rate and body temperature continuously and by connecting it to a medical grade smart watch for easy display of vitals and storing of medical sheets. For the personal health aspect it will take the collected structured data and use unsupervised machine learning to better assess an astronauts health. This project takes continuous data currently using deque collection to minimize storage use and continuously we want it to send updates using deep space networks. The benefits that the device has is quick and effective, easy to follow medical data sheets that allow for independent health administration and health testing allowing for further independence from Earth.

While it's not currently implemented, we wanted to add features for mental health as that is just as important. In doing so we believe there should be guides that are able to walk someone through mindfulness techniques such as CBT, DBT, and proper breathing techniques when necessary. A concept we also wanted to introduce  is “message of the day”. This would be a community involvement initiative that would allow people on earth to send in positive messages to support the astronauts in space. These messages at random selection would then be displayed on the watch. We figured that this idea could help with defeating feelings of isolation, but also allows opportunity for the people back on earth to find interest in S.T.E.M and Space. 

We wanted to help progress the bounds of deep space missions, keep a strong focus on independence, while also offering easy medical care systems that don’t jeopardize the effectiveness of medical assistance.

All of our coding was done in python specifically in Wing IDE. Other than the coding everything else presented was on google services (docs, slides, drive, etc.).

Our project is creative because we limited the use of AI, its only use on this project was learning how to upload our code to GIT HUB. This allowed us to have a better understanding of the code our project runs on and take creative solutions to problems we found along the way. It was more fun to make the slideshow for our presentation ourselves rather than have AI generate it for us. It felt like we were making more progress by doing our project by hand and even if it ended up less elaborate than some other projects we still ended up with a strong and unique foundation.

Our team considered factors that there are other devices already in use for the system that we are implementing. CSA uses a shirt monitoring device which effectively collects the exact vitals we described above. Our goal was to try and find the weak points in these already implemented models. In this case in deep space missions it does not resolve time delayed communications. It can also only be worn for so long before it has to be disposed of, which requires a disposal container that has to be burnt up in earth's atmosphere. This requires a lot of extra baggage, which our design would mitigate. We also considered the limitations of our own design, this included battery life, and storage. With continuous data transfer and vital data not being stored locally it would improve this problem. Within medical grade watches some have a battery life span similar to the CSA’s monitor shirt use span, if not longer than which allows our idea to have some weight into the problem.
